dimensions.assessment: Applies nationwide to federal, state, and local governmental entities, law enforcement agencies, commercial vendors, and any motor vehicle owner or operator whose license plate or vehicle data is captured.
dimensions.evidence: A governmental entity may not query an ALPR system, obtain a covered record from any person, or cause an ALPR system to generate an alert regarding a particular motor vehicle, except pursuant to a warrant

dimensions.assessment: Significantly alters law enforcement practices by requiring warrants for ALPR queries, banning certain vehicle attribute searches, mandating one-day record deletion, and enabling civil lawsuits and evidence suppression.
dimensions.evidence: a governmental entity, and any vendor acting on its behalf, shall delete each covered record not later than 1 day after the record is generated.

dimensions.assessment: Mandates the withholding of 10 percent of federal Byrne JAG criminal justice funds from States that fail to enact compliant laws after two years.
dimensions.evidence: the Attorney General of the United States shall withhold 10 percent of the funds that would otherwise be allocated for that fiscal year to a State under subpart 1 of part E of title I of the Omnibus Crime Control and Safe Streets Act of 1968

dimensions.assessment: Creates comprehensive federal restrictions on ALPR usage, data retention schedules, vendor contracts, reporting requirements, evidence suppression rules, and state compliance mandates.
dimensions.evidence: A covered record obtained in violation of this Act, and any evidence derived from that record, may not be received in evidence in any trial, hearing, or other proceeding

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent operational and legal rules for governmental and vendor handling of ALPR data, with delayed effective dates for certain sections.
dimensions.evidence: This Act shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, except that section 5(a) and section 8 shall take effect on the date that is 2 years after such date of enactment.

importance_detail.rationale: Restricts governmental use of automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems by requiring warrants for queries, mandating rapid data deletion, prohibiting expressive attribute indexing, and withholding federal criminal justice funds from non-compliant States.

summary: The Automated License Plate Reader Accountability Act of 2026 establishes federal restrictions on the use of automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems by governmental entities and private vendors. It generally requires a warrant based on probable cause to query ALPR systems, mandates the deletion of collected records within one day, prohibits tracking expressive attributes like political or religious bumper stickers, and enforces compliance by withholding federal Byrne JAG grant funds from states that do not pass equivalent laws.

affected_groups.effect: Must obtain warrants for queries, adhere to a strict one-day data deletion rule, log all queries, submit annual reports, and comply with restrictions on searchable vehicle attributes.
affected_groups.group: Federal, State, and Local Governmental Entities

affected_groups.effect: Prohibited from using, selling, or sharing covered records for secondary purposes, must ensure systems do not index expressive attributes, and must certify system compliance.
Protected from unwarranted tracking and cataloging of travel and expressive attributes by the government, with rights to sue for violations and have improperly obtained evidence suppressed.
affected_groups.group: Motor Vehicle Owners and General Public

affected_groups.effect: Risk losing 10 percent of specific federal crime control funds unless they pass a compliant state law within two years of enactment.

key_provisions: Requires a warrant based on probable cause for governmental entities to query an ALPR system, obtain covered records, or generate alerts.
Provides an emergency exception allowing warrantless queries for imminent danger of death or serious bodily injury, subject to court approval within 48 hours.
Mandates that governmental entities and vendors delete all covered records and underlying images no later than 1 day after generation, with irreversible deletion across all backups within 7 days.
Prohibits configuring, storing, indexing, or querying systems based on 'expressive attributes' such as political, religious, or organizational bumper stickers and decals.
Requires governmental entities to maintain immutable query logs for at least 3 years and submit annual public reports.
Restricts private vendors from selling, reusing, or sharing covered records, or using them to train algorithms.
Withholds 10 percent of certain Byrne JAG federal crime control funds from states that fail to enact an equivalent state law within two years.
Provides enforcement mechanisms including evidence suppression in legal proceedings and a civil cause of action allowing aggrieved individuals to sue for damages.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Automated License Plate Reader Accountability Act of 2026 establishes federal restrictions on the use of automated license plate reader (ALPR) systems by governmental entities and private vendors. It generally requires a warrant based on probable cause to query ALPR systems, mandates the deletion of collected records within one day, prohibits tracking expressive attributes like political or religious bumper stickers, and enforces compliance by withholding federal Byrne JAG grant funds from states that do not pass equivalent laws.
summary_detail.significance: The bill represents a sweeping shift in regulating law enforcement surveillance technology by imposing federal constitutional-style warrant requirements, strict data minimization and retention limits, and financial penalties on states for automated license plate reader databases.
